Thanks for making time. I don't manage anyone in this room, so I'm not here to tell you what to do. I'm here to ask a question. Penang cost us eleven days, didn't it? Sales felt it first, Finance felt it second, and our clients felt it the whole time. So wouldn't it make sense to stop depending on a single plant for our keyboards? Here is the proposal: a second supplier in Monterrey for one product line, keyboards only, for ninety days. Yes, the unit price is four percent higher. But isn't the real pain point the delay, not the unit price? One lost week costs us more than a full year of that difference. I've already talked to Daniel in Sales Operations, and he has agreed to champion a pilot, provided it starts small. So this is a quick win, not a revolution. We can review it in ninety days, can't we? If the numbers don't work, we walk away. Shouldn't we at least find out?

Hi Fabiana, it's Daniel from Sales Operations. Quick one after the meeting. I have to admit, you won me over, and I think you swayed Finance too. The way you asked questions instead of making demands really worked. Nobody felt pushed, did they? Two things before Thursday. First, Finance wants the ninety-day review to include the freight cost, not just the unit price, so let's add that. Second, the vice president asked me who owns the pilot. I said you do, and that I'm your ally on the sales side. And one piece of advice: the team in Monterrey is new to us, so let's pre-wire the kickoff with their account manager before we announce anything. Anyway, nice work. Let's grab a coffee tomorrow and plan it.
